brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.evidence: There are two keyhole hangers, accessory:0#0,0#4 and accessory:0#1,1#4. They sit on the matching back faces of the two end cells, which line up in one wall plane. The middle cell is held between the two hung cells by jointBolt:0#0,0#0 and jointBolt:0#1,0#5. The configurator checks fit, not how much weight the hangers can hold.
There are three bins: bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0 and bin:1,1,0. Each is a hex-bin-full-div3 with 3 compartments, giving 9 spice slots.

The divided bins can hold small spice containers. I couldn't show it with props: the catalogue has no spice jars, and nothing else fit the 45 mm-wide compartments. I haven't checked whether particular jar sizes fit the compartments.

finish.summary: I built a wall-hung spice rack from three hex cells joined in a shallow zigzag: (0,0), (1,0) and (1,1), all on level 0. Each cell holds a full-depth bin with 3 compartments, so there are 9 spice slots. The cells at the two ends each have a keyhole hanger (hex-acc-keyhole) on the same back face, which faces bearing 210°. Those two faces line up in one plane, so the rack sits flat against the wall. The middle cell has no hanger. It sits half a cell forward of the wall and is held between the two hung cells by joint bolts. I first tried a straight row of three, but on a hex grid the back faces of a straight row are staggered and wouldn't sit flat on a wall, so I rebuilt it as the zigzag. Every other open face has a solid end cap and the joints are locked: 20 parts, about 1.7 kg of filament. check_build reports no rule issues and the mesh-collision check reads clear. There are no props: the catalogue has no spice jars, and nothing else fit the 45 mm-wide compartments (spoons hit the cell wall). The configurator only checks fit, so whether the hangers and printed parts can carry the weight of full spice jars is unknown.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
